items.claim: 10:1-10:3 is one setting unit. The regnal dateline of 10:1 opens it, 10:2 ties the mourning to the time just named, and the completed three weeks of 10:3 close it. The edge at 10:3/10:4 has a close (the fast fulfilled) and an onset (a day-and-month date with a new place), but the onset is a calendar date and not a dateline, so medium_low is the honest grade.
items.both_sides: Onset 9:27/10:1: 9:27 ends the speech on the seventy weeks and 10:1 carries the book's last regnal dateline. Close 10:3/10:4: 10:3 completes the three weeks; 10:4 gives a day and month with no year word and moves to the river. Both sides speak at both edges; the second is the thinner.

items.claim: device_notes states, under the tier EXTRACTED, that the translation at 10:19 gives the greeting and stops, and that the Hebrew clause in which Daniel is strengthened and asks his lord to speak has no English counterpart. That is false. The WEB witness carries the second half of 10:19 on a continuation line after a paragraph break inside the verse. The tier is stronger than the evidence and the layer holds the opposite fact. The boundary itself is unaffected: the close at 10:19 is the seer's request, on both faces.
items.both_sides: Onset 10:14/10:15: the first speech is over; 10:15 resumes and the seer goes mute. Close 10:19/10:20: 10:19 ends with the seer's request that his lord speak; 10:20 answers with a question that frames the long speech. The close joins a request to its answer, so it is two-sided but soft, and medium_low stands. No cut is proposed.

suggested_fix.fact: the translation does render the second half of 10:19: after a paragraph break inside the verse it has Daniel strengthened and asking his lord to speak, so the close can be cited from both faces and no gap in the English is to be reported

The rival at 10:21/11:1, with its PE, is the strongest one and is named. This is the weakest finding of the cluster: the run crosses the opening of the quoted speech.

Close 11:1/11:2: 11:1 is a retrospect in the speaker's own voice, a dateline inside speech; 11:2 opens with 'and now' and the truth promised at 10:21. The rival edge 10:21/11:1 has a PE after 10:21 (single witness) on one side and a year formula inside speech on the other. No cut is proposed.

items.claim: The rejected alternative is not stated at its strongest. The row declines an edge at 11:19/11:20 because it would leave 11:20 as a one-verse unit. It would not have to: 11:20 can open the following unit, which then runs 11:20-11:28, nine verses, inside the size the book's plan allows. On that reading the fall at 11:19 closes a career and the succession formula at 11:20 does what it does elsewhere, open. The row as cut ends on a verse that begins with an onset formula, and its close-side warrant cites that formula as close evidence. I do not find the form evidence strong enough to move the cut, so the cut and the medium_low grade stand; the field should name the real rival.
items.both_sides: Edge as cut, 11:20/11:21: close side, the short reign is ended inside 11:20 (web:Dan.11.20 “within few days he shall be destroyed”); onset side, the succession formula at 11:21. Rival edge, 11:19/11:20: close side, 11:19 ends a career (web:Dan.11.19 “he will stumble and fall”); onset side, the same formula at 11:20. Each edge has a close and the same onset formula. What separates them is where the one verse 11:20 goes, and either way it sits in a unit of seven to nine verses.

suggested_fix.fact: an edge at 11:19/11:20 need not isolate 11:20: joined forward, 11:20 opens a nine-verse unit ending at 11:28, with the fall of 11:19 as the close before it and the second formula at 11:21 inside it; that is the rival to weigh, and the close-side fact in 11:20 is the reign's end, not the formula
